name: Journey
description: One day, Pak Chanek who is already bored of being alone at home decided to go traveling. While looking for an appropriate place, he found that Londonesia has an interesting structure. According to the information gathered by Pak Chanek, there are $$$N$$$ cities numbered from $$$1$$$ to $$$N$$$. The cities are connected to each other with $$$N-1$$$ two-directional roads, with the $$$i$$$-th road connecting cities $$$U_i$$$ and $$$V_i$$$, and taking a time of $$$W_i$$$ hours to be traversed. In other words, Londonesia's structure forms a tree. Pak Chanek wants to go on a journey in Londonesia starting and ending in any city (not necessarily the same city) such that each city is visited at least once with the least time possible. In order for the journey to end quicker, Pak Chanek also carries an instant teleportation device for moving from one city to any city that can only be used at most once. Help Pak Chanek for finding the minimum time needed. Notes: Pak Chanek only needs to visit each city at least once. Pak Chanek does not have to traverse each road. In the journey, a city or a road can be visited more than once.
input_specification: The first line contains a single integer $$$N$$$ ($$$1 \le N \le 10^5$$$) — the number of cities in Londonesia. The $$$i$$$-th of the next $$$N-1$$$ lines contains three integers $$$U_i$$$, $$$V_i$$$, and $$$W_i$$$ ($$$1 \le U_i, V_i \le N$$$, $$$1 \le W_i \le 10^9$$$) — a two-directional road that connects cities $$$U_i$$$ and $$$V_i$$$ that takes $$$W_i$$$ hours to be traversed. The roads in Londonesia form a tree.
output_specification: Output one integer, which represents the minimum time in hours that is needed to visit each city at least once.
approach_summary: Define tree DP state dp[u][state] computing optimal subproblem values for the subtree rooted at u. Aggregate transitions across children in post-order traversal in O(N × S) time.

topic_editorial.title: Editorial: 1725J — Journey [463. DP on Trees and DAGs]
topic_editorial.summary: Tree Dynamic Programming with post-order traversal.
topic_editorial.key_invariant: A rooted tree has a clean hierarchical structure: removing the root decomposes the tree into independent disjoint subtrees. Therefore, the optimal solution for a subtree rooted at vertex $u$ depends purely on the solutions of its direct children $v \in \text{children}(u)$.
topic_editorial.solution_walkthrough:
### Step 1: Root Selection & State Definition
Arbitrarily root the tree at node $1$. Define:
- $dp[u][0] = $ optimal value for the subtree of $u$ if node $u$ is excluded.
- $dp[u][1] = $ optimal value for the subtree of $u$ if node $u$ is included.

### Step 2: Post-Order DFS Traversal
We traverse the tree using depth-first search. A node $u$ computes its answers only after all its children $v \in \text{adj}[u]$ have computed theirs:
$$\text{dfs}(u, \text{parent})$$

### Step 3: Subtree Transition
For each child $v$ of $u$ ($v \ne \text{parent}$):
$$dp[u][0] = \sum_{v} \max(dp[v][0], dp[v][1])$$
$$dp[u][1] = \text{val}[u] + \sum_{v} dp[v][0]$$

### Step 4: Final Answer
At the root:
$$\text{Ans} = \max(dp[1][0], dp[1][1])$$
topic_editorial.complexity_analysis:
- **Time Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N)$
  Each node and edge in the tree is visited exactly once during the DFS traversal. All transitions at node $u$ run in time proportional to its degree. Summing across all vertices: $\sum \text{deg}(u) = 2(N-1) = \mathcal{O}(N)$.
- **Space Complexity:** $\mathcal{O}(N)$
  Adjacency list storage takes $\mathcal{O}(N)$ memory, DP state arrays take $\mathcal{O}(N)$ memory, and the DFS call stack takes at most $\mathcal{O}(N)$ depth in the worst case.
